name: Zapier
look: Warm cream canvas and deep coffee ink, one saturated orange CTA, and a 12px middle radius throughout.

hero.title: Connect your apps and automate the boring parts
hero.sub: Eight thousand apps, joined together by anyone who can describe what they want to happen. No developer required, and no ticket to raise.

features.title: A trigger, then some steps
features.sub: Every automation is the same shape, which is why non-developers can build them and still trust them.

items.title: Triggers
items.body: Something happens in one app — a form is submitted, a deal moves, a file lands.

items.title: Actions
items.body: Then things happen in others, in order, with the data mapped between them.

items.title: Paths and filters
items.body: Branch on a condition so one automation handles several cases without duplicating it.

items.title: Schedules and delays
items.body: Run on a timer, or wait a day before the follow-up so it does not arrive at midnight.

items.title: Errors you can see
items.body: Failed runs held with the data attached, replayable once you have fixed the cause.

items.title: Shared with the team
items.body: Automations owned by a team rather than by whoever happened to build them.

showcases.title: Built by the person with the problem
showcases.body: The people who know a process is tedious are rarely the people who can write a script. Handing them a builder they can actually use removes months of queueing behind an engineering backlog.
points: Built by the person who owns the process
Handed over cleanly when they leave

showcases.title: Failures are held, not dropped
showcases.body: When a step fails the run is held with its data intact rather than discarded. Fix the cause, replay it, and nothing is lost — which is the difference between an automation you trust and one you check every morning.
points: Failed runs held with data intact

gallery.title: INTEGRATIONS
gallery.sub: Eight thousand apps, and the popular ones are properly supported.

testimonial.quote: Our operations manager automated the thing she had been asking engineering for since January. It took her an afternoon and she has since built nine more.
testimonial.name: Daniel Reyes

pricing.title: PRICING
pricing.sub: Free to start. Priced on tasks, not on people.

items.a: Each successful action a step performs. Triggers and filtered-out runs are not counted, so a heavily filtered automation is cheap to run.
No. Team plans include unlimited users; you pay for tasks. That is deliberate — automation gets more valuable the more people can build it.

items.q: What if an app I need is not supported?
items.a: There are webhook and HTTP steps for anything with an API, and a developer platform for publishing a proper integration.

items.q: What happens when a step fails?
items.a: The run is held with its data rather than discarded. Fix the cause and replay it; nothing is lost in the meantime.

cta.title: Automate something today
cta.sub: A hundred tasks a month free, and the first one takes about two minutes.

footer.tagline: Connect your apps and automate the boring parts.

notes: The canvas is warm cream, not pure white. The temperature is the brand voice.
Ink is a deep coffee rather than black, and that warmth carries through every neutral in the ladder.
One saturated orange is the conversion signature and appears nowhere decorative.
12px is the middle-radius signature for both buttons and cards — neither sharp nor pill.
Every neutral in the greyscale carries warmth; introducing a cool grey anywhere breaks the temperature.
